newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Stg downside seen limited to 2.8650 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Stg downside seen limited to 2.8650 marks.

text.p: Sterling is vulnerable to a short-term correction against the mark, but any slippage will be limited to 2.8650, analysts said.

Though sterling/mark has set new 59-month highs against the mark on five out of the past six trading days, its inability to sustain gains above 2.8820 suggests its rally has run out of steam for the time being.

"The 2.8820 level seems to be pretty important and given that we have tested it twice but not held it, there is likely to be some short-term selling pressure," said Hans-Guenter Redeker, analyst at Chase Investment Bank.
"But the first support should be at 2.8650," he said.
This level marks the lows of June 24 and 26, and in the longer-term charts is a 61.8 percent retracement of sterling's fall from the highs in early 1989 to a record low in 1995.
Sterling/mark was quoted at 2.8761/71 at 0745 GMT from 2.8753/58 late Thursday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6661/71 from $1.6660/65 yesterday.

Sterling losses below 2.8650 marks would pave the way for further slippage to 2.8440/50, analysts said. This area proved to be a significant resistance between June 13 and 18, and should now offer good support.
Cable has been trading in an ever-narrowing range this past week after setting a five-month high of $1.6725 on Monday.

"Cable was relatively flat yesterday, and the downside is still open in this one," said Gerry Celaya, the senior technical analyst at American Express Bank. Still, he said there was good support at $1.6600/20.
Sterling has probed $1.6600 three times this past week but quickly rebounded on each occasion.
Analysts are therefore looking for the pound to use this level as a base to mount a fresh attempt to break through congestion at $1.6710/20.
"A break of $1.6725 suggests a move to $1.6830, represented by trendline resistance intervening on daily charts," said technical analysts at Chase Investment Bank.
"A daily closing price above here will again underscore bullishness suggesting a move above the $1.7160 December high." -Swaha Pattanaik, London newsroom +44 171 542 6284
